videos.t: Building a Nixie Clock from a Vintage Computer | Build Log
videos.desc:
I stumbled across this old computer module while digging through electronics scrap, so I figured, why not turn it into something cool? By combining a modern Nixie tube driver board, an Arduino, and some original nixie tubes, I ended up with a cool clock module with a proper, Nuclear Silo aesthetic. 

If you want to make your own Nixie Clock from scratch, check out my other video where I outline how to make a Nixie tube driver board, housing and more:
https://youtu.be/KeYZJDFRkJ0

videos.desc:
Thank you to @PCBWay ⁠ for sponsoring this build! To get started with 3D printed/CNC projects of your own, visit: https://pcbway.com/g/t3VlYi

The first phase of the Condiment Cannon build involved making a launcher mechanism out of two 2800W brushless motors to test if they could successfully launch condiment packets. Check out the full build video for more.

videos.t: Condiment Cannon: Electronics #3dprinting #arduino
videos.desc:
Thank you to @PCBWay ⁠ for sponsoring this build! To get started with 3D printed/CNC projects of your own, visit: https://pcbway.com/g/t3VlYi

To allow for semi and fully-automatic firing on the condiment cannon, I programmed an ESP32 S3 Zero to cycle a 12V solenoid at precise intervals that allowed each round of jelly to advance into place within the magazine. For added flair, I also used an OLED display to show how many rounds had been fired, as well as the battery life of the LiPo cells.

I built the entire Condiment Cannon model in CAD first before 3D printing out the frame and using PCBWay to CNC mill the motor mount. From there, I sanded all the parts and used filler primer before painting everything.

videos.t: Adding a dehumidifier to my Bambu AMS #3dprinting
videos.desc:
3D Printing filaments have to be kept at very low humidity, and I got tired of always having to cycle silica gel through my Bambu AMS to keep it dry. With this M-1J1R membrane dehumidifier, I now have a maintenance-free way to keep moisture out of my filaments. Best of all, this uses the 24V that's already run to the AMS, so there's no need to run separate cables in order to power it.

Parts list:

Solid-State Dehumidifier:

https://micro-dehumidifier.com/product/m-1j1r/

Voltage Regulator:

https://a.co/d/cBAQsbT

Cover:

https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:6814688
